answer: Practically, the chain should bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because harbor only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, basalt is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any grove approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
